title: Generating Synthetic Data for Lexical Semantic Change Detection Over Multiple Time Periods
venue: CLiC-it 2026 (Twelfth Italian Conference on Computational Linguistics), Palermo, 14-16 Sept 2026; CEUR

selection.evidence: Linked from the SemEval-2027 Task 3 competition page (News, 1 Oct 2026) as the organisers' recommended development data and its paper; read because arena-lsc competes in that task.

cost.compute_notes: PDF (13 pp) read in full. Deposit (sentences.zip 31 MB, metadata.zip 2 MB) downloaded and converted to the Task 3 format (300 random lemmas, seed 0). XL-LEXEME fp16 embeddings of 86,106 sentences on an RX 6700 XT (~8 min), once L2-normalised and once raw. Reanalysis scripts r01-r03 run on CPU (<5 min each).

triggers: synthetic data for semantic change over many periods

claims.statement: A synthetic multi-period English corpus: for 2,768 OED lemmas (13,762 senses), sense priors from a random same-polysemy SemCor lemma (tiers top/mid/low), per-sense time series from a random CCOHA word of that tier, masked to the OED attestation interval, log2(x+1) and normalised per 20-year bin (1810-1990); 30 sentences per lemma and period generated by Janus.
claims.scope: Construction only. The deposit contains metadata for the sense time series and the generated sentences with sense ids; 4,692 files.

our_assessment.why: Matches the deposit: 300 sampled lemmas give 86,106 sentences (54 dropped for bad offsets), <= 300 per lemma, 30 per period where the lemma exists. The sense dynamics are proxies (a random CCOHA word's frequency curve), so 'change' here is frequency drift of arbitrary words, not semantic history; fine for calibrating a pipeline, not evidence about how real senses evolve.

claims.statement: On the synthetic data, Spearman of predicted change vs gold JSD (first period vs each later period, averaged over 9 periods): PRT 0.473, cluster-JSD at agglomerative threshold 0.32 0.408, APD 0.297, cluster-JSD at 0.50 0.266; PRT is the most robust metric.
claims.scope: XL-LEXEME embeddings; all lemmas whose first period is 1810-1829; linkage not stated.

our_assessment.why: Pre-registered reproduction (arena-lsc ticket Literature: success if the paper's value lies in my bootstrap-over-lemmas 95% interval) on 261 lemmas (random 300, seed 0, first period 1810): APD 0.264 [0.157, 0.367], JSD@0.32 0.386 [0.301, 0.470], JSD@0.50 0.249 [0.145, 0.354] all contain the paper's values; PRT 0.367 [0.267, 0.447] does NOT contain 0.473. Not explained by normalisation: PRT from raw vectors is 0.366 [0.269, 0.460] (norms 30.6 +- 0.29; per-row difference <= 0.002, r03). With PRT reproduced lower and JSD@0.32 at least as high, 'PRT performs most robustly' is not supported on this sample; against the sentences' own sense counts (what a system sees) JSD@0.32 0.459 > PRT 0.433. Their 0.32 vs 0.50 contrast for JSD reproduces clearly. Untested causes: their exact lemma set, linkage, and PRT implementation.

claims.statement: The JSD threshold calibrated on synthetic data transfers to real OED attestations (240 lemmas, 1810-1910 vs 1911-2010): JSD@0.32 0.464, PRT 0.431, JSD@0.50 0.391, APD 0.242; 0.31 best for matching the number of OED senses on both synthetic and real data.
claims.scope: Two-period real OED data; the OED attestations are not in the deposit.

our_assessment.why: OED data not deposited (licensed), so not reproducible here. Consistent with my public-data sweeps (arena-lsc): the 1b-optimal average-linkage threshold on 8 human-annotated sets is ~0.26-0.38, the 1a-optimal ~0.40-0.50.

claims.statement: Reproduction of Table 2 on a random 300-lemma sample of the deposit (261 lemmas starting in 1810): APD, JSD@0.32 and JSD@0.50 averages fall inside my bootstrap 95% intervals; PRT (0.367, normalised or raw vectors) falls below the paper's 0.473.
claims.scope: XL-LEXEME fp16 (tooling/embed.py in arena-lsc), average linkage, gold q(t) rebuilt from the metadata per Section 3.4 (masked, log2(x+1), no log for 2-sense lemmas).

our_assessment.why: Reader's own computation; scripts and outputs in reanalysis/ (r01 point estimates, r02 bootstrap, r03 raw vs normalised). Limits: a 300-lemma subsample, linkage assumed, the paper's lemma set and PRT code unknown.

checked.how: sh .claude/memory/maria/arena-lsc/tooling/fetch_public.sh; python .../tooling/convert_public.py synth <x/synth> <gold/synth300> --code EN --words 300 --seed 0; official SemEval-2027 Task 3 scorer controls (gold 1.0, random-within-gold-k 1b rho 0.477)
checked.result: usable; 54 of 86,160 sampled sentences have offsets outside the text; the metadata frequency fields allow rebuilding the gold distributions q(t)

relations.why: Uses Janus (introduced with the hypothesis-driven framework line of work) and its 0.5 threshold as the literature default.

open_questions: Why does PRT reproduce at 0.367 and not 0.473? Ask for the exact lemma list and the PRT code; or rerun on all lemmas (needs ~2,300 x 300 sentences embedded, ~70 min GPU).
How does the synthetic set's change signal compare with the SemEval-2027 Task 3 test (real, 6 languages)? Only after the task, with the organisers' permission for test analyses.
